A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CARI4D and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. All 14 pages in each version, including eight figures and five tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on BEHAVE and InterCap, qualitative results on internet videos, ablations and oracle experiments in Tables 1–4, and supplementary runtime measurements in Table 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original reconstruction experiments, qualitative results, ablations, oracle experiments, and supplementary runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 6 retain the same scale estimation, pose hypothesis selection, CoCoNet architecture and training objectives, and contact-based joint optimization.

E1.justification: Both versions train on BEHAVE and HODome and evaluate on BEHAVE, unseen InterCap, and internet videos. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: InterTrack and VisTracker in Table 1; PICO, InterTrack, and VisTracker in Tables 2 and 5. The same adaptation supplies reconstructed object meshes to VisTracker.

E3.justification: Both retain 62 BEHAVE and 22 InterCap evaluation videos, the 24-video ablation subset, first-frame SMPL alignment, Chamfer and acceleration metrics, and 3-fps key-frame comparisons with PICO. Training and optimization settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The initialization, training-alignment, and contact-optimization ablations remain unchanged in Table 3 and Figure 6. Both retain the same oracle study in Table 4 and failure cases in supplementary Figure 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, CARI4D's combined Chamfer distances remain 8.80 cm on BEHAVE and 12.88 cm on full-video InterCap evaluation; its supplementary runtime remains 45 minutes per 300-frame video.

T1.justification: The pose and mask definitions, depth-alignment equations, joint objective, and supplementary attention and loss formulations are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both retain the same novelty and contribution claims for category-agnostic, metric-scale 4D interaction reconstruction and zero-shot generalization. The abstract's reported 38% and 36% improvements are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of alignment, contact reasoning, and baseline failures are unchanged. Supplementary Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning detailed finger articulation and severe initialization errors under rapid motion or occlusion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page hyperlink on the title page, providing access information absent from v1. Implementation details remain identical, and both versions still describe code and pretrained models as forthcoming; the PDFs do not establish an actual release.

R1.justification: The same 75 references and research-positioning arguments are retained. Changes to bibliography citation-page references reflect text reflow, not added or removed cited works.

P1.justification: Front matter gains the project URL and updated arXiv version/date text. Body prose, terminology, headings, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added title-page link shifts Figure 1 and subsequent text flow, while printed page numbers disappear throughout. The same figures, tables, and captions remain, with limited positional changes and no redesign.

improvement.justification: The new project link offers a small resource-discovery convenience, but the scientific argument, experimental evidence, technical documentation, and limitations are unchanged. Both versions still promise a future code/model release. The link and minor layout changes do not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
